dani: Quick sanity checkwe're seeing small but persistent undercounts in billed tokens vs model-side totals for streaming calls. Looks like an aggregate compaction step is dropping fractional chunk metadata.

pradeep: Are these definitely from streaming chunk merges or from multi-part uploads? Any repro with request_id?

emily: I grabbed a sample: request_id=rid_9f3c, model=gpt-x, chunks=[12,7,6,5] total=30. Compact pipeline stores per-chunk averages across batch and writes short ints. After compaction across 8 requests we end up with 27-28 tokens depending on rounding.

dani: yeah same pattern. The compactor sums per-index after dividing by batch size, then multiplies back. That math isn't associative.

pradeep: two ways: 1) change compaction to compress per-request exact total_tokens (int32) and optionally omit chunk list from compact topic; 2) keep current compact, but write an immutable audit record with full chunk list to another topic for reconciliation. Which feels better?

emily: audit topic seems lower risk for immediate deploy. Advantage: compact remains cheap, audit holds truth. Downside: cost and retention.

dani: For reconciliation we need stable primary keys. request_id must be deterministic client-side. Currently some SDKs include a random uuid per process. We need edge to supply a globally unique request_id per user request.

pradeep: agreed. Also include final_chunk=true on the last chunk. That way the aggregator can ignore provisional totals when settling the ledger.

emily: UI impact: product wants near-real-time usage so provisional numbers are shown. But billing must only account on final settle. We'll need a settled flag surfaced in usage API.

dani: Operational constraints: audit topic retention proposed 180 days compressed, with lifecycle to cold S3 after 90 days. Any objections?

pradeep: 180 days fine. Ensure we partition by tenant/day to keep compaction jobs scoped. Also store a light index (request_id -> offset) in our metadata DB so backfills don't scan whole topic.

emily: Good call on index. Also add a checksum (xxhash64) of chunk counts in audit message to catch mid-flight corruption. If checksum mismatch, mark as corrupted and route to quarantine.

dani: Nice. How about message schema (proto sketch) for audit: message AuditMeter { string request_id; string tenant_id; int64 ts; repeated int32 chunk_counts; int32 total; bool final; uint64 checksum; map<string,string> meta; }

pradeep: That works. For compact topic we'll keep {request_id, tenant_id, ts, total_tokens, provisional_bool, billing_tags}. No chunk list.

emily: Backfill plan: read audit topic for N days, recompute totals per request_id, generate delta events to billing-reconciler topic idempotent by request_id. Start with last 30 days in dry-run.

ops-bot: Reminder: run reconciliation in --dry-run for first pass. Use --concurrency=20 to avoid thundering replays.

dani: Tests: unit for compactor arithmetic, integration test that writes streaming chunks with final flag and validates ledger accepts only final settled totals, e2e dry-run backfill with known injected discrepancy.

pradeep: Migration: deploy edge SDK change (stable request_id + final flag) behind a feature flag. Start writing both old and new keys to compact/audit with a versioned field to avoid breaking consumers. After client adoption window (2 weeks) flip reading logic.

emily: I'll coordinate console change for provisional vs settled, and add a reconciliation widget for accounting to inspect diffs.

dani: Action items: pradeep -> proto + compactor change (PR), emily -> console + backfill dry-run orchestration, dani -> retention + index plan + reconciliation job. ops-bot: schedule dry-run 2026-04-05 17:00 UTC.

pradeep: I'll open a PR today with backwards-compatible schema and a small perf test to measure audit topic throughput.

dani: Thanks. Let's reconvene after dry-run. :thumbsup:
